title: JMAP: bearer token issuance and validation
description: Add per-client revocable bearer tokens on top of HTTP Basic. Design: POST /jmap/auth/token authenticates via HTTP Basic (same CredentialStore), accepts optional JSON body {"label": "thunderbird-laptop", "expires_in_days": 90}, returns {"token": "<base64url>", "id": "<uuid>", "expires_at": <unix or null>}. Token storage: SHA-256 hash of raw token stored in SQLite table (token_hash BLOB PK, username TEXT, label TEXT, created_at INT, expires_at INT nullable). Never store raw token. All JMAP endpoints accept either Authorization: Basic or Authorization: Bearer; Bearer path looks up sha256(raw_token), checks expiry. DELETE /jmap/auth/token/:id revokes a specific token. List tokens: GET /jmap/auth/token (returns id+label+created_at, never the raw token or hash). Bootstrap: operator creates first token via CLI or dev-mode Basic. This is what RFC 8620 §2 envisions and what clients expect for persistent sessions — Basic is the bootstrap mechanism.
